target_customer: Independent creators (writers, streamers, makers) and their fans
problem: Creators earn unreliable ad income and want a simple, low friction way for fans to tip and support them.
business_model: 5% platform fee on tips, memberships and shop sales (secondary sources)

founders.name: Jijo Sunny
founders.background_notes: Secondary sources say he and his brother were creators earning modest ad income in Kozhikode, Kerala.

founders.name: Joseph Sunny
founders.background_notes: YC page bio: founder and designer.

founders.name: Aleesha John
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; another source calls her Jijo's wife.

competitors.name: Patreon
competitors.traction_then: not stated in the cited article
competitors.funding_then: $60M round led by Thrive Capital in 2017, about $450M valuation per sources

technical_complexity.rationale: Payment pages on top of Stripe; one account says the first version was built in about 30 days for about $1,600, mostly the domain.

defensibility.rationale: Features are easy to copy; the exact match domain and a friendly brand are the main assets.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copycat takeover found; the company grew to claim over 2 million creators.

market_need_then: A growing creator economy with unreliable ad income; Patreon's 2017 $60M round shows investor demand for creator payments.

branding.name_origin: The company's About page says the name was chosen deliberately to make payments feel less transactional.
branding.domain_note: Bought buymeacoffee.com; secondary accounts say most of a roughly $1,600 launch budget went to the domain.

identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly, informal, creator first, stresses privacy

branding.brand_signature: The coffee cup tip metaphor and the buymeacoffee.com URL
branding.community_and_virality: Launched on Product Hunt and Hacker News per a secondary write-up; widely used buttons on creator pages; a 2026 Onmanorama feature covers the brand.

brand_strength.rationale: The name is itself the product action, is widely embedded on creator pages, and a secondary source credits the domain and name as a growth asset.

outcome_analysis: Buy Me a Coffee grew from a roughly $1,600 build by two brothers into a platform claiming over two million creators with about 30 staff, after a small YC seed of about $150K. Growth came from a simple product, a memorable name and exact match domain, and low spend. No later priced round, layoffs or sale was found, so the evidence points to a capital efficient, brand led business.
notes: The $150K YC seed is stated by CB Insights (2019-03-18) and a Substack (May 2019), both secondary; other CB Insights investors (Globevestor, Start Up Loans, Lombardstreet Ventures, Vibe Capital) are unverified. Claims of Stripe or Aaron Levie as investors come from an AI generated page and are not recorded. Founding year conflicts (2017 vs 2018). Ko-fi existed before the batch but no dated source was opened, so it is not listed. The logo change date comes from search text of a different company's page and is low confidence.
